reference: img/lfjumbo.jpg and img/lfline.jpg (Commons 'Left Field Jumbotron at Citizens Bank Park' 2371235005 / 2372079830, April 2008), cbpimg/lfj2.jpg, img/lf2.jpg (Commons 'Left Field at Citizens Bank Park' 2372056366, April 2008, crop audit4/lf/ref_lf2_upper.png: about 8 porch rows, a walkway with a rail, Harry's raised patio, 3 navy awnings, the green channel letters on red brick, maroon X-braced legs), ref/CBP_Scoreboard_JPG.jpg and img/sb_aug08.jpg (Aug 2008 from right field), hesb/2987305440.jpg (2008 World Series night, crop audit4/lf/ref_night_board.png: the neon glowing in a band between the board and the packed porch). baseballparks.com/indepth/citizens/p2 and inquirer.com (Harry the K's, 2004-2025, was on two levels: at the back of the field-level 140s and on the upper 'Scoreboard Porch' level, built into the base of the scoreboard). Confidence: high on the composition. Medium on the absolute heights, which are measured off photos using the 97 ft cabinet as the scale.
problem: From every infield and TV view the bottom of the board rests on, or behind, the back row of the Scoreboard Porch. The whole band that framed left field in 2008 is missing: no Harry the K's awnings or patio, no green 'Citizens Bank Park' letters, no maroon legs under the board. The cause is in the geometry. Bowl.js 'lf-deck' has 12 rows (treads at 11.6 to 16.9 m, back wall to about 18.1 m, its back about 129.5 m out along the board's bearing of -36 deg). Landmarks._scoreboard() puts the board's bottom at STREET+10.5 = 17.5 m, 137.8 m out, and builds Harry's as a 9 m deep brick box under the board whose front (about 136.8 m) is 7 m behind the deck. The sightline from home (eye at 1.7 m) over the deck's back only reaches Harry's front above about 19 m. So Harry's glass (12.2-15.3 m), its 6 awnings (15.8-16.7 m) and the neon (16.5-18.8 m) are all hidden, and the bottom ~1.5 m of the board is cut off too. The hidden glass then shows up through the lower concourse (see LF07).
target: Top to bottom in the April/August 2008 and World Series photos: the board's bottom edge; 0.5-1 m of maroon X-braced legs; the green channel letters 'Citizens Bank Park' with the Citizens logo (a green 'asterisk' of 4 chevron pairs) at about 0.83 x the board width (about 24 m), letters about 2.6 m tall and the logo about 3.6 m, faces #1E9E57 with bright neon outlines (#5CFF8A glow at night), on a red-brick parapet (#8A3A2A, about 4 m) with a row of 6-8 floodlights under the board aimed at them. Then three slate-navy awnings (#2B3F57, sunlit tops about #8DA6B3), each a third of the facade, with 'HARRY THE K'S - BROADCAST BAR & GRILLE' in white on the valance and a 1 m gold medallion (#C9A44A) on each slope. Then the bar's 3 m glass storey, the raised patio with a galvanized rail and standing fans, a walkway with a rail, and the Scoreboard Porch (about 8 rows, sections 241-246) down to the GEICO/Jefferson fascia. Board bottom to the top of Harry's patio crowd measures about 21-22 ft (6.6 m) in both the August and the World Series photo. From home plate the band between the porch rail and the board's bottom edge takes up about 0.28-0.35 of the board's height (H).
fix: (1) Bowl.js _upperTiers 'lf-deck': rows 12 -> 8 (top tread 11.6 + 7x0.48 = 15.0 m), back: { height: 1.07 } as a galvanized rail instead of a wall. (2) Behind it, along offsetPolyline(lfd.front, 8x0.84 + ...): a 2.4 m walkway slab at y 15.35 and a 3.6 m patio slab at y 16.35 (box(), walkable colliders), each with a 1.07 m galvanized pipe rail (#B8BCBE). (3) Landmarks._scoreboard(): y0 = STREET+10.5 -> STREET+17.0 (about 24.0 m). The script and the tower rise with it: keep the script top at about y0+1.30H and the lamp-bank top at about y0+1.95H (LF02). Rebuild Harry's as a facade parallel to the LF wall at the patio's back edge (about 29 m behind the wall line, about 132 m out along -36 deg, local z about -5.7 instead of -1.0), with its roof running back under the board. Glass storey 16.35-19.35 m (reuse harrysGlass, emissive mix(0.05,0.35,night), darker interior). 3 awnings instead of 6 (width HW/3), with the valance text and medallion in a canvas. A parapet at 19.4-23.4 m: widen the neon quad from W*0.62 to W*0.83, raise it to y about 20.2 and add a stone coping. Two lattice() leg frames from the parapet top to y0 at the board's ends. 7 floodlight boxes on the board's bottom edge (emissive at night) and a warm wall-wash term on the parapet brick. (4) Check with __look(0,1.7,3,-50,8,-95,42): the porch rail should sit about 0.3H below the board's bottom edge on screen. Note: fff.txt gives the 'highest piece of steel: scoreboard' as 143'3". If that's measured from the street (50.7 m above the field), this puts the script about 5 m higher with a 97x79 ft cabinet. Either accept that (the proportions are what read on TV) or scale the cabinet and script about 0.9 around the board's bottom.

problem: Landmarks._scoreboard() puts TOYOTA, Choose Blue., W.B. MASON and Budweiser in a 5.6 m wide column flush against the board, inside the same dark frame. Each panel is a white lightbox about 5.6 x 6 m with plain text. Behind them, bowl._lightTower(tw.x, tw.z, STREET, LEVELS.lightTowers+6, [7,5]) builds a 7 x 5 m lattice whose light bank is a flat landscape 13 x 5.4 m slab (13 x 4 lamps). From home the ads read as a white strip glued to the board, and the tower as a thin mast poking up behind the script. At night the column is a bright white bar next to the video board.
target: The panels hang on the field face of a separate square lattice tower that rises right beside the board's center-field edge (its left columns just behind the board's edge). Tower: about 13 m wide x 6 m deep, 4 box columns with X/K bracing in about 4.5 m panels, dark maroon (#3B2226 in shade, like the board's legs), rising from Harry's roof to the lamp bank. Bank: portrait, about 10 m wide x 12 m tall, about 9 x 11 lamp heads in a cage, its top about 0.65H above the script's top (about 1.95H above the board's bottom). Panels: about 11 x 4.6 m (36 x 15 ft) each with about 1.8 m gaps showing the lattice. The top panel starts about 2 m above the board's top and the bottom one ends about 3 m above its bottom. By day the faces are light grey #C9CCCE with a dark 0.2 m border. Art: TOYOTA (red #EB0A1E ellipse logo + wordmark); 'Choose Blue.' (the IBX blue cross logo with a white figure, blue #1E5BB8 serif text, a small 'www.ibx.com' tab top right); 'WHO BUT / W.B.MASON / SINCE 1898' (red); 'Budweiser' in red script. At dusk and night the faces are dark charcoal (#1E1F22) and only the letters glow (red or blue neon).
fix: Landmarks._scoreboard(): delete the ad column (frame mesh, aq quads, adTex) and the bowl._lightTower(..., [7,5]) call. Add _boardTower(g): 4 columns via beam() (0.7 m) at local x = -(W/2+0.8) and -(W/2+13.8), z = 1 and 7. Girts every 4.5 m and one X per face per panel (0.25 m members), height to y0+1.95H. A portrait bank (10 x 12 m, 9 x 11 lamp boxes, tilted 0.3 rad toward the infield): either add a bank-size option to Bowl._lightTower (W>8 currently jumps to _portalTower) or copy its bank block, and push it to bowl.towers so the night lights use it. Panels: 4 quads, 11 x 4.6 m, on the tower's field face (z = 0.2), from y0+H+2 downward with 1.8 m gaps, each with a 1024x428 canvas drawn as above. Shader: let t = tex; let lit = step(0.3, max(t.r, t.b) - t.g); s.albedo = mix(t, t*0.12, frame.night*(1.0-lit)); s.emissive = t*lit*mix(0.1, 2.5, frame.night).

reference: hesb/2986448333.jpg (2008 World Series, crop audit4/lf/ref_ws_monty.png): fans in seats above the State Farm wall right up to the 409 marker, a rail sloping up along the top of the angle, and the ivy batter's eye starting at 409. img/lf2.jpg (April 2008, crop audit4/lf/ref_lf2_monty.png): seats behind the taller wall with a galvanized mesh rail following its slope. problem: Bowl._lowerTiers() 'left-field-seats' uses front = _fenceLine(0, 3) (pole, 334, 374, 387), so the 140s end at 387 with a sloped end wall. Behind Monty's Angle, Bowl._pitOutline() (cf = offsetPolyline(_fenceLine(3, 8), 7)) and Landmarks._battersEye() put a 7 m ivy-covered pit wall with evergreens and a bare concrete apron above it. From home and the high TV camera, left-center shows a brick wedge and a dark green box above State Farm where there should be a block of fans.
target: The left field seats wrap round over Monty's Angle to the 409 corner. The front row sits just behind the top of the taller wall (12'8" from 387 to 381, rising to 19' at 409), behind a 1.07 m galvanized rail with mesh infill that steps up along the wall top. Rows end at the Ashburn Alley walkway: about 10-12 rows at 387 thinning to about 5 at 409 (photo estimate). The angle's wall above the pads is plain flat green metal. The ivy/brick batter's eye starts only at 409 (CR01 says the same from the center field side).
fix: Bowl._lowerTiers(): add a 'monty-seats' tier: front = this._fenceLine(3, 6), outward [0,0], start 0.8, depth FROW, y0 = 12.67*FT + 0.4 (4.26 m), rise 0.2, rows 12, section 10, aisle 1.2. For the rising 381->409 stretch, either give buildTier a per-front-vertex y0 offset (wallH(p) - 12.67 ft) and drop rows whose tread would be above STREET, or split it into 3 short tiers (y0 4.9 / 5.5 / 6.1 m, rows 10 / 7 / 5). Push it into this.tiers after 'left-field-seats'. In _pitOutline() replace cf with [...back(monty), ...offsetPolyline(this._fenceLine(6, 8), 7, [0,0])]. In Landmarks._battersEye() use _fenceLine(6, 8). Extend Details2008._planters()' rail over at(3)..at(6), with its base following the wall height (OUTFIELD rows 4-6).

title: The 'Phillies' script is about half size in Georgia italic with no truss behind it, and the board is a plain navy box with no steel-blue frame or lamp arms
seen_in: audit4/lf/d-board.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=13&weather=off, __look(-20,5,-30,-81,30,-111,40)); audit4/lf/n-board.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=21, __look(-20,5,-30,-81,30,-111,40)); audit4/lf/e-like-jumbo.png (http://127.0.0.1:5193/?hour=13&weather=off, __look(10,10,10,-60,20,-105,40)) (audit4/lf/cmp-stack.jpg); steps [{"file":"cam.js"},{"file":"audit3/seg.js"},{"js":"__start()","wait":1500},{"js":"__clean()"},{"js":"__look(...)","wait":2500},{"shot":...}] (night runs add __seek(600) before the first __look)
reference: cbpimg/lfj2.jpg, img/lfjumbo.jpg, cbpimg/j1.jpg (April 2008 close-up: the steel-blue frame, ribbed siding and lamp arms), ref/CBP_Scoreboard_JPG.jpg (August 2008), hesb/2987305440.jpg (World Series night neon). Confidence: high.
problem: The sign is drawn with ctx.font 'italic 700 220px Georgia' into a 1024x320 canvas on a 0.78W quad. The lettering comes out about 61% of the board's width and about 0.16H tall. It's a book italic rather than the Phillies script, the swash is a straight bar, and it floats on 3 thin posts with no frame behind it. The cabinet is a uniform dark navy box (0.03, 0.06, 0.16) with no frame color, no lamp arms and no maker's name. At night the script's emissive tops out at 0.6, dimmer than the video board.
target: The script spans about 0.78W (about 23 m) and about 0.42H (P-top to swash bottom, about 10 m), its top about 1.30H above the board's bottom. It's the Phillies wordmark: thick brush script, a 'P' with a looping bowl, 'hillie' joined, the tail of the 's' sweeping back left under the word as the swash, and two navy #1D3F8F stars with white edges as the i-dots. Red #C8102E faces with 0.15-0.2 m cream (#F2EAD0) returns and outline, on a black-painted steel frame (#1C1A1E): two end lattice towers and a horizontal truss that show between the letters. At night it's bright red neon, the reddest thing in the park, with a white edge glow. Cabinet: a steel-blue frame (#6194B1 in sun, about 0.6 m) round each of the 4 faces (Coke, Motrin, matrix, video), ribbed blue siding on the sides, about 8 floodlights on 1.5 m arms along the top of the Coke panel and the bottom edge of the board, and 'PHILIPS' in white under the video.
fix: Landmarks._scoreboard(): sign canvas 2048x800. Draw the wordmark from an SVG path: trace the 1992-2018 Phillies script outline once into a Path2D string, stroke it in cream (lineWidth 18) then fill it red, so the letters stop depending on the system's fonts. Quad SW = 0.8W, SH = 0.42H at y0+H+0.3, keeping the 6 back layers for depth. Frame: lattice(g, blackSteel, +-0.44*SW, 0.8, y0+H, y0+H+0.8*SH, 1.4) plus a beam() Warren truss along y0+H+0.25*SH. Cabinet: 0.6 m border strips round each face in Color(0.12, 0.29, 0.43) linear, with the siding the same hue. Lamp arms: beam() arms 1.5 m long with 0.5x0.3x0.3 lamp boxes every 3.5 m on the top and bottom edges (emissive at night). Add 'PHILIPS' to drawBoard2008()'s bottom margin. Night: signMat emissive mix(0.2, 0.6) -> mix(0.3, 2.4, frame.night) so it blooms like neon.

fix: New Landmarks._lfRamp() (or in Exterior.js), built with Quads: runs as 0.3 m slabs, 3 m wide at 1:12, 30-45 m long, with 4 m 180-degree landings, stacked from STREET to LEVELS.terraceConcourse behind the corner-lf tier's back edge and the lf-deck's pole end (about x -95 to -125, z -55 to -95 in the field frame; check against FOOTPRINT and Bowl's corner tier). Steel from this.steel: 0.6 m box columns and 0.9 m deep girders. Rails from beam() plus a see-through mesh (CR05's coverage shader). Pendant lamp boxes under each run with night emissive. Trim the brick end wall so the steel reads through. Gulf: CylinderGeometry(1.75, 1.75, 0.3) with a canvas face on a post at the front of the corner deck, emissive 1.5 at night. BUBBA: two 3 x 0.8 m red boxes under the corner deck.

section: Left field: the covered concourse under the Scoreboard Porch (back of the 140s)
title: Under the Scoreboard Porch the concourse is a bright empty arcade open to the sky, and at night a glowing amber slat wall. In 2008 it was a dark covered concourse with section plates, a rail and Harry's lower bar

reference: img/lf2.jpg (April 2008, crop audit4/lf/ref_lf2_concourse.png): deep shade under the fascia, maroon columns, tan section plates '143' '144' '145' hung from the soffit, speakers and floodlights, a galvanized rail with red trash cans behind the last row. hesb/2987305440.jpg (2008 World Series night): a dark band with a few warm lights under the lit GEICO/Jefferson signs. baseballparks.com: Harry the K's lower level at the back of the field-level seats. Confidence: high.
problem: The lf-deck is 10 m deep (it ends about 26 m behind the wall line) and Harry's box starts about 34 m back, so the concourse behind the 140s is open to the sky. By day it's a bright grey arcade with a brick back wall and a navy 'Harry the K's' plaque. At night the upper Harry's glass (the harrysGlass canvas, emissive 0.6), hidden from home by the deck, shows through here as a glowing amber wall of vertical slats under the GEICO fascia.
target: A deep, dark, roofed concourse (about 15-20% of the sunlit seats' brightness) with maroon columns, and a galvanized rail with red trash cans along the back of the 140s. Tan section plates (#CDBE93 with maroon numerals '140' to '145', about 0.6 x 0.45 m) hang from the back of the fascia, one per section, with speakers and floods under the soffit. At the back is the lower level of Harry the K's: a dark glazed bar front with a lit sign and a few TV monitors. At night only small warm downlights and the bar's glow.
fix: Bowl: roof the concourse by extending the lf-deck soffit (or a slab at the deck's base level) back to the Harry's line from LF01, so no sky shows. Add a storefront quad at the back: a canvas of dark glazing (#1A1714) with a dim warm interior, a 'Harry the K's' blade sign and 3 TV rectangles (emissive 0.4). Section plates: 256x192 canvases on quads hung from offsetPolyline(lfd.front, 0.4) once per section at y = lfd.base - 0.6. The galvanized rail and red cans go along the back of the 140s. Light: multiply ambient by 0.25 in the soffit/wall/floor materials under the deck, and at night add 4000 K downlight pools every 6 m (emissive discs plus a radial term in the floor shader). Set harrysGlass night emissive to 0.25 once it moves up (LF01).

reference: img/lfpole.jpg (April 2008: a flower trough between the wall and the front row down the line), audit4/lf/ref_lf2_walltop.png and ref_lf1_walltop.png (April 2008: purple and white flowers behind the wall under a silver rail), grp/gr_p6.png (ground rule 5, 'landing in the flowerbed' is a home run: the trough with pansies, grasses and a silver rail, 2024 but the same build), fff.txt ('up to three seasonal changes of annuals'). Confidence: high on the bed and the rail, medium on the October planting.
problem: Details2008._planters() builds only a 1.05 m chain-link on a grey rail, 0.55 m behind the wall face. Its shader keeps a veil alpha of up to 0.3 and the alpha test turns the far mesh solid, so from the field it reads as a row of pale frosted-glass panels on top of the wall. There's no flower bed, even though the file's header promises 'the flower boxes on the left field wall'.
target: Directly behind the wall cap, a planted trough about 1.2 m wide runs from the pole to 387, soil about 0.25 m below the cap. Dense low annuals with a few clumps of ornamental grass; in October, pansies or mums: purple #5B2A6E, white #EFEDF2, burgundy #8E1F3A, yellow #E6BE2E. On the seat side, a 1.07 m galvanized rail (#B8BCBE): 5 cm top rail, posts about every 1.8 m, see-through picket or mesh infill. The front row of the 140s sits right behind it.
fix: Details2008._planters(): move the rail to o = 1.75 m (the seat side) and give its infill CR05's coverage alpha (at most ~0.15 at distance, never solid), or vertical pickets every 0.12 m. Add the trough: a soil quad (#3B2A20) at y0-0.25 from o = 0.3 to 1.6 m and a 0.1 m curb. Flowers as an InstancedMesh of low domes or cards (0.22 m, about 6 per m2, per-instance color from the palette, 15% grass tufts 0.45 m tall), about 350 instances from the pole to 387. Bowl leftField start 1.5 -> 2.0 so row 1 clears the rail.

reference: img/lf2.jpg (April 2008, crop audit4/lf/ref_lf2_upper.png): GEICO|GEICO|GEICO box and the blue Jefferson box on a grey fascia; cbpimg/lfj2.jpg. hesb/2987305440.jpg and hesb/2986448333.jpg (2008 World Series): both boxes lit, and the Jefferson one reads 'Jefferson University Hospitals'. Confidence: high.
problem: Fascia._lfDeck() paints the whole lf-deck front as one off-white band (#f2f1ec) with 'GEICO' three times, 17% apart, in Helvetica, plus a Georgia-serif 'Jefferson University Hospitals' box, emissive at most 0.4. From home it reads as a continuous white stripe across left field.
target: A plain light-grey precast fascia (#C4C2BB) carrying two separate backlit sign boxes. GEICO: about 12 x 1.2 m, three equal cells (white | royal blue #1F4FA0 | white) with 'GEICO' in the GEICO wordmark (heavy extended sans, blue on white and white on blue) and a navy 8 cm frame, centered about 40% along the deck from the pole end (over sections 142-143). Jefferson: about 14 x 1.6 m at the center field end, blue #2A55C0, white 'Jefferson' in bold plus 'University Hospitals' in regular (Helvetica), hanging a little below the fascia. Both lit at night.
fix: Fascia._lfDeck() canvas: fill '#c4c2bb' with light precast noise and a panel joint every 3 m. Draw only the GEICO box (u 0.30-0.48: 3 cells, 'Arial Black' stretched x1.25) and the Jefferson box (u 0.64-0.98, Helvetica bold and regular instead of Georgia). Put a mask in the alpha channel (1 inside the boxes) and use s.emissive = t*mask*mix(0.1, 1.4, frame.night). Give the Jefferson box its own quad, 0.4 m taller and 0.15 m proud of the fascia.

section: Left field foul pole and wall markings (the LF details on top of CR08/CR10)
title: The left field pole has no painted '329' and a yellow collar, the pads are 1.5 m flat panels with square tops, and the distance numbers carry a dark outline

reference: img/lfjumbo.jpg (crop audit4/lf/ref_pole_jumbo.png) and img/lf1.jpg (crop audit4/lf/ref_pole329.png), April 2008: '329' painted down the pole in black. audit4/lf/ref_lf1_walltop.png and ref_lf2_walltop.png (April 2008): pad pitch about 1.28 m with rounded tops and cream numbers without an outline. grp/gr_p25.png (2024): the green pad sleeve where the pole meets the wall. Confidence: high. Not repeated here: the pad color, the yellow top stripe (CR08) and the plank-like pole screen (CR10) come from the same code for both poles and walls, and fixing them there fixes left field too.
problem: The left field pole carries no '329' and its collar is yellow. The pads are one continuous panel with a seam every 1.5 m and a square top edge. The distance numbers (_buildDistanceMarkers) have a dark #0e2a24 outline that makes them look embossed rather than painted.
target: '329' painted vertically on the field face of the pole in black condensed digits about 0.8 m tall, stacked, with the '9' about 0.4 m above the wall top. A green vinyl pad sleeve about 0.8 m tall where the pole meets the wall. Pads about 1.28 m (4.2 ft) wide, each with a 2 cm dark seam and a rounded 6 cm top roll that catches the light. Distance numbers cream #E8DFB6 in a condensed bold sans, about 0.75 m tall, no outline: '334' just right of the pole corner, '374' left of Southwest, '387' at the corner.
fix: Field._buildFoulPoles(): for the left field pole (k === 0) add an open CylinderGeometry(0.247, 0.247, 2.9, 32, 1, true) sleeve starting at wallH+0.3, with an alpha-tested 256x1024 canvas of '3', '2', '9' stacked (black, 'Arial Narrow' 800). Rotate its u so the digits face home (the right field pole gets '330'). Collar material -> the pad material. Field._buildFence() pad shader: seam period 1.5 -> 1.28, plus a top-roll term from the height on the wall (in.P.y against the wall height h, passed in through uv.y): shade *= mix(1.0, 1.25, smoothstep(h-0.1, h-0.04, y)) * mix(1.0, 0.7, smoothstep(h-0.03, h, y)). _buildDistanceMarkers(): drop the strokeText outline, fill '#e8dfb6', and squeeze to 0.72 horizontally.
